pages.text: $(l)Traffic light$()$(br)It cycles on its own through red, then orange, then green, and starts again. Set the length of the cycle with its value box. It connects through its $(item)top$() and $(item)bottom$() faces, so you can stack it on a post, and it is a $(item)175 ohm$() consumer. It only lights up while powered.

$(l)Freezer$()$(br)Cools a chemical vat. It connects on $(item)any face$() and is a $(item)75 ohm$() consumer. It only works with $(item)more than 3 A$(), which means above $(item)225 V$(), and burns above 400 A.

$(l)Electrode holder$()$(br)Holds an electrode in a chemical vat for electrolysis. It takes power through its $(item)top$() face and needs at least $(item)5 A$() to work; its resistance depends on the electrode inside.
Both are part of the vat multiblock. See the $(item)Chemical Vats$() chapter to build one, and the $(item)Aluminium$() chapter for electrolysis.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
